headline: Approved withdrawal of 287 Crescent Street special permit change; tabled $462,755 Police Station design loan.
summary: Councillors also gave a second reading to an amendment to the Compensation Ordinance on election personnel costs. They referred the Prestige Car Wash and MICOL special permit hearings to the Ordinances and Rules Committee and recessed both to December 14, 2026. They also approved several grants and appointments and referred four Mayor funding requests to the Finance Committee.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the October 13, 2026 meeting by voice vote.
Referred the Secondhand Dealers license at 1275 Main Street to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
Referred the Secondhand Dealers license at 550 Winter Street to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
Referred the Special Permit modification at 101 Elm Street to the Ordinances and Rules Committee and recessed the hearing to December 14, 2026.
Referred the Special Permit application at 220 Moody Street to the Ordinances and Rules Committee and recessed the hearing to December 14, 2026.
Filed the Mayor's request for councillors to serve on a Hockey Rink Design Committee after naming seven councillors.
Referred the Mayor's request for $64,600 to the Finance Committee for the Lake Street Fire Station roof.
Referred the Mayor's request for $42,536 to the Finance Committee for the Farwell Street Bridge design.
Referred the Mayor's request for $56,760 to the Finance Committee for the Chester Brook Culvert project.
Referred the Mayor's request for $40,000 to the Finance Committee for services of Leanne Wilcinski.
Referred seven extended hours and Class II license applications to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
Approved the Waltham Fire Department Retirees Resolution by voice vote.
Approved the appointment of Richard Pizzi, Jr. to the Council on Aging, 12-0-2-1.
Approved the appointment of Marcia MacClary to the Council on Aging, 12-0-2-1.
Approved a $120,000 appropriation from the Cemetery Sale of Lots & Graves account for a new truck by voice vote.
Approved acceptance of a $52,152 grant for the Municipal Road Safety program by voice vote.
Approved acceptance of a $9,000 grant for new EV chargers in public parking lots by voice vote.
Approved an amendment to the Compensation Ordinance on election personnel costs for a second reading by voice vote; councillors then voted 12-0-2-1 to suspend Rule 45 for a third and final reading.
Approved a $462,755 loan authorization for Fire Administration Wing design for a first reading by voice vote.
Tabled the $462,755 loan authorization for Fire Administration Wing design on the Council floor by voice vote.
Approved the Fortune Tellers license at 24 Crescent Street by voice vote.
Approved the Extended Hours renewal at 12 Harvard Street for CVS Pharmacy #114 by voice vote.
Approved the McDevitt 8th Grade Civics Resolution by voice vote.
Approved a request that the Mayor place a set of Big Belly solar trash and recycling compactors on Moody Street.
Approved the 17-25 permit at 205 Second Avenue for NationalGrid by voice vote.
Approved the 17-25 permit at South Street and Vernon Street for NationalGrid by voice vote.
Approved withdrawal without prejudice of the Special Permit modification at 287 Crescent Street, 12-0-2-1.

plain_text:
1
Waltham City Council 
Minutes of the Meeting of 
October 26, 2026
President Logan called the meeting to order at 7:35 p.m. 
 
Artie Kronenfeld from the Waltham Times was recognized as recording the meeting.
Present: Bradley-MacArthur, Brasco, Dunn, Durkee, Harris, Hanley, King, LaFauci, LeBlanc, 
McLaughlin, Tzioumis, Vidal and President Logan. 
Absent: Katz, LaCava.
City Clerk Vizard recited the Council Prayer followed by President Logan leading all present in the 
Pledge of Allegiance. Councillor Durkee for a moment of silence for all our troops serving all over 
the world and for those supporting them.
President Logan gave an update on Councillor Katz saying he was home and recovering. Councillor
Katz was very thankful for all the well wishes.
Councillor LeBlanc moved approval of the regular City Council meeting minutes of October 13, 
2026. The motion was approved by a voice vote. 
Clerk Vizard read Rule 86.
First Public Hearing: Secondhand Dealers license at 1275 Main Street for Hits and Holos
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Michelle Tutunjian of 177 Lura Lane, Waltham, 
MA the petitioner, spoke on the matter. With no one else in favor, no one in opposition and no 
one in a neutral position President Logan closed that part of the public hearing and opened the 
hearing up to questions from Councillors. No Councillors had questions. With no further 
questions President Logan referred the matter to the Licenses and Franchises Committee. 
Councillor Vidal stated the Licenses and Franchises Committee will meet November 2, 2026 at 
7:00 p.m.
Second Public Hearing: Secondhand Dealers license at 550 Winter Street for Roadshow Concepts, 
LLC.
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Amy Morgan of 20 Olney Street, Watertown MA 
representing the petitioner, spoke on the matter. With no one else in favor, no one in opposition and
no one in a neutral position President Logan closed that part of the public hearing and opened the 
hearing up to questions from Councillors. No Councillors had questions. With no further questions 
President Logan referred the matter to the Licenses and Franchises Committee. Councillor Vidal 
stated the Licenses and Franchises Committee will meet November 2, 2026 at 7:00 p.m.
Third Public Hearing: Special Permit Modification at 101 Elm Street for Prestige Car Wash
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Attorney Jospeh Connors of 404 Main Street, Waltham,
MA representing the petitioner, spoke on the matter. With no one else in favor, no one in opposition
and no one in a neutral position to the ordinance President Logan closed that part of the public hearing
and opened the hearing up to questions from Councillors. Councillors LaCava, Tzioumis, Vidal, King
and McLaughlin asked questions. Attorney Connors supplied answers. With no further questions
President Logan referred the matter to the Ordinances and Rules Committee. President Logan
recessed the public hearing to date certain of Monday, December 14, 2026 at 7:30 p.m.
2
Fourth Public Hearing: Special Permit Application at 220 Moody Street for MICOL, LLC (recessed 
8/3/26)
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Attorney Phillip McCourt of 272 Bacon Street, 
Waltham, MA representing the petitioner, stated the petitioner was waiting for additional 
information. With no one else in favor, no one in opposition and no one in a neutral position to the 
ordinance President Logan closed that part of the public hearing and opened the hearing up to 
questions from Councillors. No Councillors had questions. With no further questions President 
Logan referred the matter to the Ordinances and Rules Committee. President Logan recessed the 
public hearing to date certain of Monday, December 14, 2026 at 7:30 p.m.
Communications from the Mayor
1. The Mayor respectfully requested the names of City Councillors to serve on a Committee 
regarding the design of a rink at the Lawrence School property. President Logan 
recommend Councillors McLaughlin, Hanley, King, LaCava, LaFauci, LeBlanc and 
Bradley-MacArthur to serve as members of the Hockey Rink Design Committee. 
President Logan moved to file the matter. The motion was approved by a voice vote and 
the matter was filed.
2. The Mayor respectfully requested a transfer of funds in the total amount of $64,600 to 
fund the roof replacement at the Lake Street Fire Station. Referred to the Finance 
Committee.
3. The Mayor respectfully requested a transfer in the amount of $42,536 for the preliminary 
design phase of the repair of the Farwell Street Bridge. Referred to the Finance 
Committee.
4. The Mayor respectfully requested funding in the amount of $56,760 to cover the expanded
scope of work required for the Chester Brook Culvert at Beaver Street Lining project. 
Referred to the Finance Committee.
5. The Mayor respectfully requested funding in the amount of $40,000 to provide for the 
professional services of the former School Department Assistant Superintendent of 
Finance and Operations, Leanne Wilcinski. Referred to the Finance Committee.
Applications and Licenses
All Applications and Licenses referred to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
1. Extended Hours renewal – 1335 Main Street – Waltham Fuel, Inc.
2. Extended Hours renewal – 677 Moody Street – MK and Company LLC
3. Extended Hours renewal – 591 Moody Street – 7Eleven Store 37504A
4. Extended Hours renewal – 573 Main Street – J&T Shun Lai, Inc.
5. Class II license renewal – 935 R MainStreet – Pilicy Auto & Yacht Inc.
6. Class II license renewal – 260 Bear Hill Road, Sute 202 – Global Lease Group
7. Class II licenses renewal – 50 River Street – Absolute Auto Sales
Resolutions, Orders and Ordinances
Waltham Fire Department Retirees Resolution
Vice President LeBlanc spoke on the Resolution. Vice President LeBlanc moved to suspend Rule
39 to act on the matter without Committee Reference. The motion was approved by a voice vote.
3
Vice President LeBlanc moved approval of the Resolution. The motion was approved by a voice 
vote and the Waltham Fire Department Retirees Resolution was approved.
Committee Reports
Committee of the Whole
1. The Committee of the Whole recommended the confirmation of the appointment of Richard 
Pizzi, Jr. as a permanent member of the Waltham Council on Aging to fill a vacancy be 
approved. Councillor LeBlanc moved that the action of the Committee be the action of the 
Council. Roll call required.
In favor: Councillors Bradley-MacArthur, Brasco, Dunn, Durkee, Hanley, Harris, King, 
LaFauci, LeBlanc, McLaughlin, Tzioumis and Vidal.
Opposed: None.
Absent: Katz, LaCava.
Presiding: Logan.
Approved: 12-0-2-1.
2. The Committee of the Whole recommended the confirmation of the appointment of Marcia 
MacClary as a permanent member of the Waltham Council on Aging to fill a vacancy be 
approved. Councillor LeBlanc moved that the action of the Committee be the action of the 
Council. Roll call required.
In favor: Councillors Bradley-MacArthur, Brasco, Dunn, Durkee, Hanley, Harris, King, 
LaFauci, LeBlanc, McLaughlin, Tzioumis and Vidal.
Opposed: None.
Absent: Katz, LaCava.
Presiding: Logan.
Approved: 12-0-2-1.
Finance Committee
1. The Finance Committee recommended an appropriation in the amount of $120,000 from the
Cemetery Sale of Lots & Graves account to purchase a new Chevrolet Silverado 3500 truck 
with snowplow package for the use of the Cemetery Division be approved. Councillor 
Durkee moved that the action of the Committee be the action of the Council. The motion 
was approved by a voice vote, and the matter was approved.
2. The Finance Committee recommended the acceptance of a grant in the amount of $52,152 
from the Office of Grants and Research (OGR) to support the FFY2027 Municipal Road 
Safety (MRS) Program be approved. Councillor Durkee moved that the action of the 
Committee be the action of the Council. The motion was approved by a voice vote, and the 
matter was approved.
3. The Finance Committee recommended the acceptance of EECBG additional grant funds in 
the amount of $9,000 from the Department of Energy for the installation of new EV 
Chargers in the City’s public parking lots project be approved. Councillor Durkee moved 
that the action of the Committee be the action of the Council. The motion was approved by a
voice vote, and the matter was approved.
Ordinances and Rules
1. The Ordinances and Rules Committee recommended the adoption of an amendment to the 
Compensation Ordinance pertaining to personnel costs associated with elections be approved
4
for a second reading. Councillor Harris moved that the action of the Committee be the action of
the Council. The motion was approved by a voice vote, and the matter was approved for a 
second reading. Councillor Harris moved to suspend Rule 45 for a third and final reading. Roll 
call required.
In favor: Councillors Bradley-MacArthur, Brasco, Dunn, Durkee, Hanley, Harris, King, 
LaFauci, LeBlanc, McLaughlin, Tzioumis and Vidal.
Opposed: None.
Absent: Katz, LaCava.
Presiding: Logan.
Approved: 12-0-2-1.
Long Term Debt & Capital Planning
1. The Long Term Debt & Capital Planning Committee recommended a loan authorization in
the amount of $462,755 for additional design services for the inclusion of the Fire 
Administration Wing of the Police Station be approved for a first reading. Councillor 
Durkee moved that the action of the Committee be the action of the Council. The motion 
was approved by a voice vote, and the matter was approved for a first reading. Councillor 
Durkee moved to table the matter on the Council floor. The motion was approved by a 
voice vote and the matter was tabled on the Council floor.
Licenses and Franchises
1. The Licenses and Franchises Committee recommended the Fortune Tellers license at 24 
Crescent Street STE 401F for Minwoo Park be approved. Councillor Vidal moved that the
action of the Committee be the action of the Council. The motion was approved by a voice
vote, and the matter was approved.
2. The Licenses and Franchises Committee recommended the Extended Hours renewal at 12 
Harvard Street for CVS Pharmacy #114 be approved. Councillor Vidal moved that the 
action of the Committee be the action of the Council. The motion was approved by a voice
vote, and the matter was approved.
Public Works and Public Safety Committee
1. The Public Works and Public Safety Committee recommended The McDevitt 8th Grade 
Civics Resolution be approved. President Logan relinquished the Chair to Vice President 
LeBlanc. President Logan spoke on the matter. President Logan made a request that was 
approved by a voice vote to respectfully request that Her Honor, The Mayor of Waltham, 
arrange for a set of Big Belly solar powered trash and recycling compactor be placed on the
sidewalk on the West side of Moody Street near the entrance to the DCR River Walk, as 
suggested by the students at the McDevitt Middle School 8th Grade Action Civics Project. 
Councillor Dunn moved that the action of the Committee be the action of the Council. The 
motion was approved by a voice vote, and the matter was approved.
Vice President LeBlanc relinquished the Chair back to President Logan.
2. The Public Works and Public Safety Committee recommended the 17-25 at 205 Second 
Avenue for NationalGrid be approved. Councillor Dunn moved that the action of the 
Committee be the action of the Council. The motion was approved by a voice vote, and the 
matter was approved.
5
3. The Public Works and Public Safety Committee recommended the 17-25 South Street and 
Vernon Street for NationalGrid be approved. Councillor Dunn moved that the action of the 
Committee be the action of the Council. The motion was approved by a voice vote, and the 
matter was approved.
Unfinished Business & Other Business
1. Councillor Harris moved to suspend Rule 43 to allow a late filed communication regarding the 
motion to withdraw without prejudice the Special Permit modification at 287 Crescent Street, 
Waltham, MA. Councillor Harris moved to suspend Rule 39 to act on the matter without 
Committee reference. The motion was approved by a voice vote. Councillor Harris moved for 
approval of the matter. Roll call required.
In favor: Councillors Bradley-MacArthur, Brasco, Dunn, Durkee, Hanley, Harris, King, 
LaFauci, LeBlanc, McLaughlin, Tzioumis and Vidal.
Opposed: None.
Absent: Katz, LaCava.
Presiding: Logan.
Approved: 12-0-2-1.
Tabled Items
 66 Brewster Road (Tabled 6/9/25)
Rule 58
 Communication regarding the Trapelo Road Shuttle Service (Resolution to Explore 
Transpiration Options in North Waltham).
Recessed Public Hearings
 Special Permit Modification Dyer’s Crescent Suites, LLC 287 Crescent Street recessed 
9/14/26 (11/23/26)
 Special Permit Modification Service Credit Union 995 Main Street recessed 9/14/26 
(11/23/26)
 Special Permit Application 20 Williams Street recessed 9/28/26 (11/23/26)
 Special Permit Application Sweetgreen Boston, 96 Tower Road recessed 10/13/26 
(11/23/26) 
With no further matters Councillor Brasco made a motion to adjourn. The motion was approved 
by a voice vote. President Logan declared the meeting adjourned at 8:32 p.m.
Respectfully submitted by:
Cathy Magliarditi
Executive Assistant to the City Clerk
November 3, 2026
